title: The Optimal Biological Therapy for Conversion in Patients with RAS Wild Type Colorectal Cancer and Unresectable Liver Metastases
content: Background/Objectives: The treatment goal for patients with unresectable liver-limited metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is resection. Biological agents directed to vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) and epidermal growth factor receptor (anti-EGFR) are effective in RAS wild type mCRC. We aimed to investigate which type of biological therapy is more efficient and tolerable in the first line treatment of patients with RAS wild type mCRC and unresectable liver metastases. Methods: This was a prospective, single-centre cohort analysis that included patients with mCRC and unresectable liver metastases, without mutations in the KRAS and NRAS genes (exons 2, 3 and 4), treated at the University Clinical Centre of Nis, Serbia. The overall response rate (ORR), depth of response (DoR), resection rate (RR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were compared between patients treated with the anti-EGFR antibody cetuximab/panitumumab and those treated with the anti-VEGF antibody bevacizumab, each in combination with the chemotherapy doublet FOLFOX/FOLFIRI. Results: Fifty-one patients were treated with anti-EGFR antibodies and 50 patients received bevacizumab. Anti-EGFR treatment provided better ORR (70.6% vs. 50%; p = 0.034), deeper response (47.2% vs. 33.67%; p = 0.004) and higher RR (66.7% vs. 46%; p=0.036). Median PFS was significantly better in the anti-EGFR treated group (12.1 vs. 8.5 months; p=0.016). Median OS tended to be better in anti-EGFR-treated patients, but the difference was not significant (30.4 vs. 25.5 months; p=0.221). Both treatments had comparable rates of grade 3/4 toxicity (37.2% vs. 28%; p=0.32). Conclusion: Patients with RAS wild-type, unresectable mCRC should be treated with anti-EGFR therapy when aiming for conversion.
